extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community, grant-funding researchers, and policy analysts studying funding disparities
extracted.subtask_description: Re-analysis of NIH R01 applications (2011–2015) to evaluate whether topic choice, peer review outcomes, and Institute/Center (IC) award rates explain race-based funding disparities, focusing on first-time (de novo) submissions. Uses topic assignment (Word2vec), descriptive statistics, regression, and predicted-vs-actual award rate comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAB preference for each topic (P_AAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: P_AAB = (∑_{i=1}^{n} aab) / (∑_{i=1}^{N} aab) — proportion of all AAB applications within a topic (Equation 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify how skewed AAB PI applications are across topics; treated both as a continuous variable and categorically (topics among the top set accounting for 50% of AAB applications designated 'AAB Preferred'). Figures and regressions examine associations between P_AAB and peer review/funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/Center (IC) award rate (A_IC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A_IC = (number of applications funded in IC) / (number of applications assigned to IC) (Equation 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC award rates vary (observed 6% to 15%) and are a primary explanatory variable: used directly in regressions, and to predict topic award rates; adjusting for A_IC reduced the AAB PI coefficient substantially (14% reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific observed award rate (A_t)
rubrics_metrics.description: A_t = (number of applications funded in topic t) / (number of applications in topic t) (Equation 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual topic-level funding outcome used to compare with predicted award rates derived from IC award rates (Equation 4) to evaluate whether topic assignment to ICs explains observed funding differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted topic award rate (Â_t)
rubrics_metrics.description: Â_t = ∑_{i=1}^{n} Â_i where Â_i is the award rate of the IC to which application i is assigned (Equation 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents expected topic award rate if funding probabilities were determined solely by IC-specific award rates; compared to observed A_t to assess role of IC assignment in topic-level funding differences (strong correlation r=0.62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of applications discussed (D_t)
rubrics_metrics.description: D_t = (∑_{i=1}^{n} d) / n, where d is indicator whether application i was discussed (1 if yes) (Equation 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-review outcome capturing the first hurdle; used to compare peer-review selectors across topics and AAB preference (e.g., no significant negative association between P_AAB and D_t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific mean priority score (s̄_t)
rubrics_metrics.description: s̄_t = (∑_{i=1}^{l} s) / l where s is priority score of discussed applications (range 10(best)–90(worst)) (Equation 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean used to compare peer-review quality across topics; percentiles also used to account for peer-review group calibration differences. Regression of mean score on topic size used to control for regression-to-the-mean effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of 'AAB Preferred' topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics among those that together account for 50% of all AAB PI applications (15 topics out of 148 in primary analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a categorical indicator (AAB Preferred vs Other) in descriptive tables and regressions; authors also examine alternative cut-points (e.g., 70% => 37 topics) and treat AAB preference continuously to test sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on de novo (first-time) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analyses restricted to applications submitted to NIH for the first time (excluded resubmissions and competing renewals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: resubmissions and renewals systematically fare better on peer review and would bias comparisons; resubmission analyses presented separately (Appendix 1) with similar conclusions but different baseline award rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probit regression model of funding (Equation 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Y_i = β_0 + β_1 PI_AAB + β_2 TAABP + β_3 A_IC + β X + ε — modeling probability of funding with covariates (Equation 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI_AAB indicator, topic AAB Preferred indicator, IC award rate, and X (Early Stage Investigator status, multi-PI indicator, human/animal subject indicators). Model comparisons use AIC, BIC, and Log Likelihood; key inference: adjusting for IC award rate reduces race coefficient most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of covariates (X): ESI, multi-PI, human/animal subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: X corresponds to variables including 'Early Stage Investigator' status, whether application designated more than one PI, and whether the proposed research involved animal and/or human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These covariates are included in extended models (Table 6 Model 3) to control for factors known to affect funding probability; ESI defined as PI within 10 years of terminal degree/clinical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression of mean score on topic size and weighted residuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear regression of topic-specific mean priority score on topic size (number of discussed applications) to predict mean; residual = observed minus predicted mean; residuals weighted by topic size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts for regression-to-the-mean (smaller topics have greater variance); weighted residuals prioritize larger topics' information when comparing AAB Preferred vs other topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of priority scores and percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority scores (10 best–90 worst) assigned to discussed applications; many applications also receive percentile rankings to adjust for differences in reviewer calibration across peer review groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses compare both median priority scores and percentile rankings across topic groups and IC groups to assess whether peer-review outcomes differ by topic or PI race.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and suppression for privacy (cell size rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data for ICs with cell sizes not exceeding 11 are not shown due to privacy concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic/ reporting constraint affecting tables and figures; reviewers and readers should note suppressed small-cell data when interpreting IC-level summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic assignment via Word2vec algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application was designated to one of 148 topics identified by the Word2vec algorithm (as in Hoppe et al., 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic topic assignment underlies topic-level analyses; authors note original Hoppe et al. reported 150 topics but found data processing errors leaving 148 for re-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC assignment process (CSR Division of Receipt and Referral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to ICs based on IC interests, specific Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs), and sometimes applicant request (CSR, 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC assignment drives the 'funding ecology' effect; assignment (including occasional dual assignment) is a procedural determinant of which IC award rate applies and is therefore central to explaining topic-linked funding disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of withdrawn and non-reviewed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 2% of applications are withdrawn prior to review for administrative reasons; only discussed applications receive priority scores (about half of non-withdrawn applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors exclude pre-review withdrawals from denominators in main analyses and focus on those applications that go through peer review; be aware of attrition before discussion when interpreting rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of p-values, regression coefficients with standard errors, and conventional significance annotations (*** p<0.001; ** p<0.01; * p<0.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results report both statistical significance and effect sizes (e.g., reduction in absolute value of race coefficient when adjusting for topic or IC award rate). Authors also report correlation coefficients (r) and p-values for descriptive associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection criteria: AIC, BIC, Log Likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Akaike Information Criteria (AIC), Bayesian Information Criteria (BIC), and Log Likelihood values used to inform model strength and comparisons across probit specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower AIC/BIC and higher log-likelihood indicate better model fit; authors present these metrics across models to justify inclusion of IC award rate and covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of 'Higher AAB' ICs
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs in the top quartile of proportion of applications with AAB PIs were labeled 'Higher AAB' (6 out of 24 ICs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare review and funding outcomes (Table 2); authors test sensitivity to alternative groupings and discuss rationale and limitations of categorical cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses: resubmissions and single-PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses repeated focusing on resubmission applications and separately on single-PI applications to assess robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission analyses (Appendix 1) show similar patterns though with higher baseline award rates; single-PI analyses (Appendix 2) also yield similar conclusions, addressing concerns about multi-PI attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of R and reproducible code/data
rubrics_metrics.description: All analyses used R packages (tidyverse, ggplot2, finalfit, texreg); de-identified data frame (.RData) and R markdown files provided as supplementary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and reproducibility: source data and code are available to reproduce main paper and appendices; readers can replicate and test alternative cutoffs or model specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive rubric: separating peer-review outcome from IC funding ecology
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors evaluate whether lower funding for AAB-preferred topics is due to peer-reviewer bias (differences in discussed proportion, priority scores) versus assignment to ICs with lower award rates (funding ecology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude peer-review outcomes are similar across topic types while IC award rates largely explain observed funding disparities; recommended analytic approach: compare peer-review metrics and then adjust funding regressions for IC award rate to assess mediation.
